title: Introducing Dixieland at Harmon's ballroom and winning over the welfare worker
summary: Elgar's five-piece band went on trial against Mrs. Bimford's objections, won over the young dancers, and grew to fifteen.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, I went in with Patty with five pieces. That's when the craze of Dixonland music had just begun to hit Chicago. And I went to see him and ask him if he'd give me a chance with this outfit. At that time he had an 18 piece white orchestra. Frank Cavallo had the orchestra there. And he kind of hesitated for a minute because he didn't know how people would go for it. And I was fortunate enough to sell him on the idea of giving it a trial, which he agreed to do. Well, we went in there with the understanding that if the thing didn't go over and if the authorities didn't, because there was no such thing in any ballroom in Chicago prior to this time. He said, now, there was a Mrs. Bimford who was a welfare worker. He said, now, she comes in here all the time and if she doesn't go for this type of thing, she says, I'll have to let you go. I said, it's perfectly all right. I'm willing to take my chances. Well, we went in there as a trial. About the second week, she came in there and began to say that our type of music was a little too boisterous for the young people. Too rough.
Rough. Who was in the band, do you remember?

We had Joe, the same boy. See, I didn't change very much. You didn't change? No, no, no. Those boys stayed with me right on through. The clarinet, do you remember? I was playing Clown Insect for myself. Oh, you were playing Clown Insect for yourself. Yeah. And after the second week, he said, well, I'm afraid we're going to have to dismiss you because she's complaining too much. I said, well, that was the agreement, it's all right. Well, we were there just long enough to have won over the young dancers, all of the young people. At that time, they were mostly young Jewish people, Italians, from over in that area. And they all went for our type of music. And they started complaining about when you're going to get this band back, when you're going to get this band back, when you're going to get this band back. So after about a month, here comes a telephone call. He said, you better come over here and let me have a talk. I said, I'll go back over there and have a talk on it. He said, well, we're going to make another stab at it and see what happens. Well, it was funny. He said, I'm going to let you see who Miss Bimford is. And whenever you see her come in that door, regardless of which you play, you start playing a waltz. And I followed instructions. And finally, we see her come in and she'd sit around there, maybe sometimes a half hour, maybe an hour. We didn't play anything but the sweetest type of foxtrot, you know. Then we finally won her over. See, well, that was the story. After we did that, well, there was no more trouble. In the meantime, why, Paddy decided that he wanted to increase the band and we kept on adding first one and then we had another until we had, from five, we had increased the orchestra to 15 pieces.
Was the bandstand right at that corner, like there's Van Buren and the...
No, the bandstand was, the bandstand was about the center of the hall. If you remember, that hall was a whole block long.
But right inside, remember, then the elevator went right over that one corner.

No, at that corner there was where the bar was on one side and the office was on the opposite side. But the bandstand was way up about the center and in the later days, it was in the center of the floor. Right in the very center, the people used to dance around us.
Yeah, I remember now seeing a picture with Jimmy Lee sitting on the... That's right. ...and that's when Cook was there.
We had a picture there with Charlie Cook because Charlie Cook followed me in there. I've seen that picture. Well, that was put right in the center of the ballroom.
Yeah, that's what it does look like, that one I think. Yeah. I guess I remember. Well, that's just a great place, isn't it?
Yeah, we spent so many very happy hours there.
